description.text: Carlyle is one of the world’s largest global investment firms that deploys private capital across three business segments: Global Private Equity, Global Credit, and Carlyle AlpInvest (formerly, Global Investment Solutions). Our teams invest across a range of strategies that leverage our deep industry expertise, local insights, and global resources to deliver attractive returns throughout an investment cycle. Since our firm was founded in Washington, D.C. in 1987, we have grown to manage $477 billion in AUM as of December 31, 2025. Our experienced and diverse team of more than 2,500 employees includes 770 investment professionals in 27 offices across four continents, and we serve more than 3,200 active carry fund investors from 87 countries. We seek to invest with a clarity of purpose, adaptability, and alignment between our interests and the interests of our fund investors, shareholders, and other stakeholders. Operational and strategic highlights for our firm and our three global business segments for 2025 include: •Assets under management grew 8% to $477 billion as of December 31, 2025 from $441 billion as of December 31, 2024. The increase was driven by inflows of $53.7 billion during 2025, a 32% increase from 2024. We deployed $54.5 billion across our platform during 2025 and realized proceeds of $34.1 billion for our carry fund investors. •We returned approximately $0.9 billion in capital to our shareholders.

analysis_md:
# CG — Carlyle Group Inc.
Engine 5.4 run, 2026-10-17. Sector: Finance / Alternative Asset Management. Price $36.38 (nasdaq_quote_api, key_numbers.md). Market cap $13.494B (key_numbers.md) — in scope under $40B.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json or statements.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
One of the world's largest diversified alternative asset managers, in three segments: Global Private Equity, Global Credit, and Carlyle AlpInvest (secondaries / co-investment / portfolio finance). Total AUM was a record $485.5B at June 30, 2026, with fee-earning AUM of $334.4B (segment AUM: Global Credit $211.1B, Global Private Equity $162.7B, AlpInvest $111.7B). The manager's own economics are management fees, fee-related performance revenues and realized carried interest on other people's capital — reported by the company as segment fee-related earnings (FRE) and distributable earnings — while its GAAP statements consolidate a slice of the funds (including CLO vehicles) whose assets it manages. (Fortitude Group, the reinsurance platform Carlyle advises, is not one of the consolidated entities — it appears in the 10-K only in AUM contexts, its general-account assets sitting inside fee-earning AUM under the strategic advisory services agreement.) That consolidation gap is the whole story of this run. Q2 2026 was a record quarter on the manager's own basis: FRE $358M (+11% YoY, 47% FRE margin), distributable earnings $472M ($1.07/share, the highest in nearly four years), $16.8B of inflows in the quarter and $56B over twelve months, dividend held at $0.35/share.

## Owner's earnings
- **Conservative OE (OCF − capex − SBC), FY2025:** OCF -$3,275,500,000 − capex $99,400,000 − SBC $374,700,000 = **-$3,749,600,000 = -$10.11/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $-10.11, latest FY OE total $-3.750B). OE was positive in only **1 of the last 5** fiscal years on this definition (key_numbers.md).
- **Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC):** $901,400,000 for FY2025 (financials_history.csv) — it collapses toward GAAP net income ($808,700,000 in the same file) and inherits the GAAP marks on consolidated investments; it is not used as the base, but the gap between the two definitions (roughly +$0.9B vs -$3.75B on the same year) is itself the cleanest single exhibit of the model misfit below.
- OE/share history (financials_history.csv): FY2021 $4.3757 (the one positive year in the last five), FY2022 -$1.5693, FY2023 -$0.3066, FY2024 -$3.5462, FY2025 -$10.1091. The series tracks consolidated-entity investment flows, not fee earnings: on the company's segment basis in the same 10-K (MD&A), FY2025 total segment revenues were $3,901,500,000, distributable earnings were $1,691,200,000 and fee-related earnings were $1,236,200,000 (a record, +12% YoY) while standardized OE printed its worst year in the window.
- **Base used = the engine's normalized base: $-3.55/share, median of the last 3 FY OE/share** (key_numbers.md: base OE/share $-3.55, source median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share; the median and the normalized figure are the same $-3.5462302178855363 in dcf_numbers.json). No override is declared: a base built on the manager's FRE / distributable earnings is not available within the bounded override authority, because a `base_override` may be built only from figures this run's dcf_numbers.json / ttm.json / financials_history.csv printed, and FRE appears in none of them. The standardized base is therefore kept for comparability and the misfit is carried in the flags, the confidence and the verdict — the same discipline as the ARES and BEN passes, except that here the standardized base is negative, so the standardized verdict is F.
- **TTM base — run, quoted, and NOT used.** ttm.py (filing-direct) legs: OCF FY -$3,275,500,000 − prior YTD -$520,900,000 + current YTD -$1,242,900,000 = **TTM OCF -$3,997,500,000**; capex FY $99,400,000 − prior YTD $34,200,000 + current YTD $60,100,000 = **TTM capex $125,300,000**; SBC FY $374,700,000 − prior YTD $196,400,000 + current YTD $235,800,000 = **TTM SBC $414,100,000**; shares (current-YTD weighted diluted) **368,081,014**. **TTM OE total -$4,536,900,000 → -$12.33/share.** The TTM window is worse than the fiscal year on the same consolidated-flow artifact (H1 2026 consolidated OCF was -$1,242,900,000 while Q2 2026 FRE set a record), so pinning the base to TTM would deepen a spurious F, not correct one. The median base is used and the TTM result is reported here as evidence about the OCF definition.
- Balance sheet: see DEBT_TAGS_BLANK below — the engine's net debt is not reported (key_numbers.md: net debt —), and no leverage figure is quoted from the engine.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate
CAP = clamp(2 + 1.3 × 5) = **8.5 years** (key_numbers.md: moat 5/10, CAP 8.5 yrs, terminal growth 2.50%; growth holds 2 years, then converges to 2.5% over the CAP, 15-year projection — moot for the score, see DCF).
Evidence first (fundamentals.json): there is no filed return-on-capital or gross-margin series to quote — `roic_proxy` is null in every annual year (the filer captions no operating income; operating_income is null throughout financials_history.csv) and `gross_margin` is null from FY2018 onward (no COGS caption is filed). A moat of 7 or above needs ROIC that stayed well above the cost of capital through a cycle; that evidence does not exist in this filer's statements, so the score rests on the segment record instead: FRE margin of 47% in Q2 2026 and record FRE in both FY2025 ($1.2B) and Q2 2026 ($358M) show a real, recurring fee profit pool, while the moat_against items below cap it at moderate.
- FOR: Scale and diversification — $485.5B total AUM and $334.4B fee-earning AUM at June 30, 2026 across Global Private Equity ($162.7B), Global Credit ($211.1B) and Carlyle AlpInvest ($111.7B), so no single strategy or vintage carries the firm
- FOR: Recurring fee engine is growing — record fee-related earnings of $358M in Q2 2026 (+11% YoY, 47% FRE margin) and record FRE of $1.2B in FY2025 (+12% YoY) on the company's segment basis, with distributable earnings of $472M ($1.07/share) in Q2 2026
- FOR: Sticky long-dated capital and fundraising momentum — $56B of inflows over the twelve months to Q2 2026 ($16.8B in the quarter), $28B of pending fee-earning AUM, and a rapidly growing wealth channel (Evergreen wealth assets +60% YoY to $20B)
- FOR: Sustained capital return on the manager's own cash earnings — $0.35/share quarterly dividend ($1.40 TTM DPS in fundamentals.json), dividends paid TTM $504,500,000 and buybacks TTM $915,300,000
- AGAINST: No structural pricing power — LPs re-bid every vintage competitively among Blackstone, KKR, Apollo, Brookfield, Blue Owl and Ares; Carlyle wins allocations, it does not set the fee rate, and credit spreads have compressed as rivals scaled
- AGAINST: No measurable ROIC or gross margin in the filings — operating income and COGS are not captioned (roic_proxy and gross_margin are null throughout fundamentals.json), so there is no filed return-on-capital series that stayed above the cost of capital through a cycle to underwrite a higher score
- AGAINST: Earnings geared to the fundraising / exit cycle — performance revenues and marks swing GAAP revenue violently (FY2021 $8,782,100,000 to FY2023 $2,963,900,000 in financials_history.csv) and a closed exit market hits realizations, fundraising and marks at once
- AGAINST: Consolidated balance-sheet opacity — GAAP OCF is dominated by consolidated fund / insurance-entity flows (FY2025 OCF -$3,275,500,000 vs net income +$808,700,000), consolidated-fund liabilities sit inside total liabilities of $22,058,900,000 with no engine-readable debt tag (the 10-K face shows corporate Debt obligations of $2,997,000,000 and Loans payable of Consolidated Funds of $10,426,000,000, neither captured by the engine's debt tags), and SBC is heavy and recurring ($374,700,000 in FY2025, $414,100,000 TTM)

## DCF — Tier F: no scenario table exists, and that is the finding
The engine's Tier F branch fired: the normalized base is not positive, so no scenarios, IVs, or IRRs are computed (score.json: implied_irr null, iv_at_15 null). Probabilities recorded for the run: 10/25/30/25/10 (defaults — nothing in the evidence justifies tilting weights for a branch that does not use them).
- **F sub-type: no_cash_generation** (key_numbers.md; f_subtype_basis: sum of the last 3 fiscal years, the median window). FCF legs from financials_history.csv: FY2023 +$138,300,000, FY2024 -$837,200,000, FY2025 -$3,374,900,000 — the window's OCF − capex is not positive. On this filer the sub-type label describes the standardized cash-flow definition, not the manager's cash generation: the same FY2025 paid $505,100,000 of dividends and $686,500,000 of buybacks (financials_history.csv) out of segment distributable earnings the OCF line does not measure.
- **Growth sanity check:** the engine's blend is 2.03% (key_numbers.md: rev CAGR 5y 10.25%, rev CAGR 3y 2.50%, latest rev YoY -11.91%, OE/share CAGR 2y not computed; share count CAGR 0.47%, growth adj -0.47%). Every component is a GAAP-revenue artifact for this filer (see BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT): the prints that describe the manager's earnings — FRE +12% in FY2025, FRE +11% YoY and distributable earnings per share $1.07 in Q2 2026 — are segment figures, not inputs to any scenario the engine can run on a negative base. Written reason, as the spec requires: growth applied to a negative base produces no valuation in any case, and no growth input changes this tier.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago): ttm.py was run and its full legs are quoted in the OE section; its TTM base (-$12.33/share) was NOT used, for the documented reason that its OCF leg is the same consolidated-flow artifact, worse in the TTM window (TTM OCF -$3,997,500,000) and contradicted by every manager-earnings print in the same window (record Q2 2026 FRE of $358M, distributable earnings $472M). The median-of-3-FY base is used instead. Q2 2026 (10-Q filed 2026-08-10) is the latest quarter.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT** (>60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs): identified — it is performance-revenue and investment-mark volatility in the GAAP revenue line, not a divestiture, acquisition restatement, or basis change in the fee business. GAAP revenue ran $2,934,600,000 (FY2020) → $8,782,100,000 (FY2021, a strong carried-interest / realization year) → $4,438,700,000 (FY2022) → $2,963,900,000 (FY2023) → $5,425,800,000 (FY2024) → $4,779,800,000 (FY2025) (financials_history.csv), and a single quarter shows the mechanism: Q3 FY2025 GAAP revenue was $332,700,000 vs $2,635,200,000 in Q3 FY2024 (fundamentals.json quarterly) on unrealized marks, while segment revenue in that quarter was $782.5M on the company's basis. Consequence: no GAAP revenue CAGR (5y 10.25% / 3y 2.50% in key_numbers.md) is trusted as a run-rate for anything, and no scenario growth was anchored to one.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income and OCF differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025): structural for a consolidating alt manager, not a one-off. FY2023 net income -$608,400,000 vs OCF +$204,900,000; FY2024 net income +$1,020,400,000 vs OCF -$759,500,000; FY2025 net income +$808,700,000 vs OCF -$3,275,500,000 (financials_history.csv). The FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement (pp. 155–156) names the driver exactly: purchases of investments by Consolidated Funds of $11,700,400,000 against proceeds from sales and settlements of investments by Consolidated Funds of $6,413,400,000 — a net consolidated-fund investment outflow that GAAP runs through operating activities and that swamps the manager's own lines (the statement starts from total net income of $944,700,000 including noncontrolling interests; the filer's own non-consolidated investment activity in the same section was purchases of $403,600,000 vs sale proceeds of $832,900,000). No insurance or reinsurance balance-change line appears in the operating section — Fortitude is not consolidated (see What it is). The mirror image is on the financing side: FY2025 financing cash flow was +$3,990,400,000 (financials_history.csv) while the standardized debt-issued line is only $90,000,000 (statements.json) — consolidated-fund borrowings and noncontrolling-interest financing, not corporate borrowing. Consequence: neither GAAP net income nor consolidated OCF is the manager's distributable earnings; the OCF-based base is treated as a standardized screen that fails this filer outright (negative), the maintenance definition (~net income) is reported for contrast, and the verdict is Tier F on the screen with the misfit stated, at low confidence.
- **DEBT_TAGS_BLANK** (no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN, not zero): confirmed from the engine's outputs and then resolved from the face of the FY2025 10-K Consolidated Balance Sheets (p. 152, filed 2026-02-27). Filing-direct totals (financials_history.csv / statements.json, Dec 31, 2025): cash and equivalents $1,970,200,000, restricted cash $3,400,000, total assets $29,116,000,000, total liabilities $22,058,900,000, total equity $7,057,100,000 (including non-controlling interests in consolidated entities of $1,295,600,000), PPE net $224,900,000. The 10-K face breaks the liabilities out: corporate **Debt obligations $2,997,000,000**; **Loans payable of Consolidated Funds $10,426,000,000** (with other liabilities of Consolidated Funds of $1,260,400,000 — fund/CLO obligations, generally non-recourse to the manager); accrued compensation and benefits $5,849,400,000 (the seasonal bonus accrual, the largest single liability after fund loans); accounts payable, accrued expenses and other liabilities $543,700,000; lease liabilities $470,200,000; due to affiliates $203,900,000; deferred revenue $129,200,000; deferred tax liabilities $106,300,000; accrued giveback obligations $72,800,000. The balance sheet also carries $1,235,100,000 of cash held at Consolidated Funds and $12,519,800,000 of investments of Consolidated Funds, which are fund assets, not the manager's. No separate Fortitude or insurance-related liability line appears on the face — Fortitude is an advisory/AUM relationship, not a consolidated liability. Resolution: the engine reports no net debt because none of these lines reaches its LongTermDebt tag (total_debt is null in fundamentals.json for every year after FY2016), so **no engine leverage verdict is taken**; on the filing face, corporate debt obligations of $2,997,000,000 stand against the manager's own cash of $1,970,200,000 — modest corporate leverage, with the $10,426,000,000 fund-loan figure belonging to consolidated funds rather than to a solvency claim on the manager.
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (Finance — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low): the controlling flag, and for CG it is not a caveat on a usable number — it is the reason the number is negative. Carlyle is an asset manager, not a lender: capex ($99,400,000 in FY2025) and SBC ($374,700,000) are real costs of the manager, but consolidated OCF is not the manager's cash flow at all (see NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE), so OCF − capex − SBC capitalizes consolidated-fund plumbing. Confidence is **low** per the rule, score.json records model_fit "misfit" and suppresses any alert for that reason, the standardized base is kept for comparability, and no tier_override is taken: Tier F is already the conservative end of the screen, and upgrading it on a non-standard FRE base is outside the worker's bounded override authority (see OE section). The F therefore reads as "not scoreable on standardized OE," not as "the business generates no cash" — the manager's segment FRE was a record $1.2B in the same FY2025 whose standardized OE is -$3,749,600,000.

## Thoughts / overlay
- **Method range (the real headline):** on the standardized consolidated-OCF definition every variant is Tier F — normalized median base -$3.55/share, latest-FY base -$10.11/share, TTM base -$12.33/share. On the maintenance definition (NI-based, $901,400,000 in FY2025) the earnings sign flips positive but the figure inherits GAAP marks and is not an owner's-earnings base this screen can capitalize. On the manager's own segment definition — FRE of $1.2B in FY2025 growing +12%, distributable earnings of $472M in Q2 2026 alone — the business is plainly cash-generative, pays a $1.40/share annual dividend and bought back $915,300,000 of stock TTM (fundamentals.json); a DCF on that definition is a different model, not a variant of this one, and building its base is a main-agent decision, not a worker override. Anyone quoting this Tier F without the misfit attached is hiding the ball in the opposite direction from the usual one.
- Quality on the manager's own terms is genuinely improving: record AUM ($485.5B) and FRE, Global Credit and AlpInvest at record distributable earnings in Q2 2026, $56B of LTM inflows, pending fee-earning AUM of $28B (+57% YoY) as a visible future fee pipeline, and a fundraising super-cycle claimed by management into 2027–28 as flagship funds return to market. None of that is measurable in OE terms on this screen, and none of it is priced here.
- Risks to monitor on the manager's own terms: a private-credit default wave hitting Global Credit (now the largest segment at $211.1B) and consolidated-fund marks at once; fundraising cyclicality if allocators pause; performance-revenue lumpiness if exit markets close (Q1 2026 GAAP revenue missed heavily on unrealized marks before Q2 reversed it); SBC scale ($414,100,000 TTM and rising with headcount in wealth / AI initiatives); and the stock's own de-rating — at $36.38 it sits near its 52-week low after trading near $69.85 within the last year, which says the market is pricing the cycle risk, not the FRE record.
- **Hurdle math:** none exists on this screen — a negative base computes no IV and no hurdle-clearing price (score.json: iv_at_15 null, implied_irr null). The name does not clear 15% at any price *on current standardized OE numbers*, which is a statement about the definition, and it should be re-scored on the standardized screen only when a filed year prints positive consolidated OCF − capex − SBC, or sooner if a main-agent FRE-based base is authorized.
